focus: Q1: what Lane C parity measured and what a restore would need
noveltyJustification: First pass: established the harness's comparison contract, its three honesty guards, its five statuses and the full restore inventory from the deleted-module history.
answeredQuestions: KQ-1 (partial: measure contract established; restore inventory enumerated)

finding: Lane C parity compared the live compiled decision (public front door, SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=1) against the Mode A legacy replay per playbook scenario.
Three guards: vacuous-parity (manifest servingAuthority must read compiled), shape bridge via qualifiedIdToLeaf against the destination hub's manifest, frozen-scorer digest pin.
Verdict = routing-projection equality (action, selectionKind, ordered targets) plus gold outcome equality on routes; shared gold failure on matching routing is parity, not drift.
Five per-scenario statuses (match/drift/vacuous/n-a/resolver-missing); rollup broken > drifted > serving; named owner lane-c-compiled-parity; outer BLOCKED-BY-COMPILED-DRIFT.

Defer/none/unknown map to empty expected intents; holdout is excluded from the fitted aggregate; negative scenarios measure forbidden/suppression waste; resource gold is exact-assembly (sk-doc shape) or must-include+no-forbidden-prefix (sk-code shape).

Restore needs 4 modules + vitest + orchestrator YAML + fixture/docs corpus + shared frontmatter parser + leaf-resource-contract + status probe/front door; the three frozen scorer files are SHA-256 digest-pinned and any edit forces re-pinning.

Retirement was deliberate and broad: five entry points, workflow contracts, script tree, fixtures and typed ledgers removed; recorded as a capability loss with a manual-playbook wrapper that cannot be rehomed as it stands.
Parity never measured hub selection (compiled routes only within an identified hub), live Mode B dispatch, or freshness repair.
